question: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q3 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)

calls.reasoning: Reference: NVIDIA's recent guide midpoints run ~11.5-12.3% above prior-quarter actuals, with guide-to-guide steps of +$13B (78->91) and +$17B (91->108). Q3 actual likely ~$112-115B, given typical beats of 4-6% on the guide. A ~12% step from there gives a midpoint of ~$125-129B. Sell-side consensus for the January quarter is ~$125B, and Wedbush expects a $124-130B guide. NVDA has recently guided ~3% above consensus. Downside: supply/memory constraints and a possibly conservative interim CEO (Kress) after Huang's resignation. Upside: Vera Rubin ramp and hyperscaler re-acceleration. No human market on the Q4 guide; the Polymarket Q3 Data Center contracts (a different quantity) imply DC revenue of ~$105-106B, consistent with a Q3 beat.

- Wedbush expects a Q4 FY27 guide of $124-130B, midpoint ~$2B above consensus (futunn, Nov 2026).

calls.reasoning: Q3 actual is likely ~$113-114B: the Polymarket DC ladder implies a DC median of ~$105-106B at ~93% of revenue, consistent with 5-6% beats on the $108B guide. Recent next-quarter guides ran 1.115-1.145x the just-reported actual, giving ~$126-129B. Escalating guide steps (+13, +17) point to ~$127B. Consensus for the Q4 actual is ~$125B and Wedbush expects a $124-130B guide. Interim CEO Kress after Huang's resignation adds a modest conservative tail, but she has long set guidance as CFO and supply commitments are locked in.
calls.reconciliation: The runs differed mainly on Q3 actual (111 vs 113-115) and how much interim-CEO conservatism to price. The Polymarket DC ladder quoted in the dossiers (54% >105B, 30% >110B, 1% >115B) implies Q3 DC ~105-106B, so total ~113-114B. That favours runs 1 and 2 over run 3's lower Q3 assumption. Ratio history and consensus (~$125B; Wedbush $124-130B) are undisputed across dossiers. The CEO effect is pure judgment: Kress authored prior guides, so I priced it as a fatter low tail (p_below 5%) rather than a lower median. No web access this run; nothing retrieved.

disagreements.verdict: Not yet knowable. The Polymarket DC ladder plus ~93% DC share and beat history centre it at ~$113-114B; residual uncertainty is carried in the width.
All dossiers agree on the three historical ratios; I used the range 1.115-1.13.
